Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

link noun and verb

a connection between things or people

also bond, family ties, be linked, linked to

classical

Cic. Off. 1.50: ejus autem vinculum est ratiō et ōrātiō
Cic. Arch. 2: habent quoddam commūne vinclum

vinculum (vinclum), vinculī n.

noun, second declension

a bond, a link

Literally a band or a tie; Cicero’s word for what holds things or people together.

Other words

  • conjūnctiō, conjūnctiōnis f. — a connection, a joining

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.50: societās hominum conjūnctiōque

  • conjungō, conjungere, conjūnxī, conjūnctum — link, join together

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.50: conjungitque nātūrālī quādam societāte

    See also connect.

Examples

  • etenim omnēs artēs quae ad hūmānitātem pertinent habent quoddam commūne vinclum et quasi cognātiōne quādam inter sē continentur

    for all the arts that belong to a liberal education have a kind of common link, and are held together, as it were, by family tiesCic. Arch. 2

See also connect, link.

SourcesLewis & Short: vinculum · Lewis & Short: conjunctio · Lewis & Short: conjungo
